claims.text: The baseline is a uniform high-entropy alloy with a conventional composition lacking targeted oxide-promoting additions.
Adding targeted oxide-forming elements promotes formation of a robust mixed oxide layer on the alloy.
The compositionally promoted mixed oxide layer is more adherent than the baseline oxide layer.
Passivation by the mixed oxide layer limits corrosion.
Improved oxide-film adhesion increases resistance to mechanically induced film removal and wear.
The added oxide-forming elements produce an in-situ mixed oxide passivation film.
The compositionally promoted mixed oxide layer is self-healing.
The mixed oxide layer remains more adherent under mechanical stress.
The mixed oxide layer reduces corrosion by preventing direct electrolyte contact with the underlying alloy.
The mixed oxide layer reduces abrasive wear by acting as a physical barrier.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the modified alloy will have lower wear-volume loss than the baseline.
Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, the modified alloy will have lower corrosion-current density than the baseline.
The protective benefit will be most notable when wear and corrosion are concurrently active.
The benefit may diminish or vanish when mechanical loading exceeds the adhesion strength of the oxide film.
The benefit may diminish or vanish in environments that inhibit oxide formation.
Trade-offs between mechanical properties and oxidation kinetics may affect performance under extreme conditions.
